name: furze

attributes.attribute: yellow blossoms for much of the year
made people mistake furze gold for metal

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Furze is a thorny plant that grows in Irish bogs. Yellow blossoms with a vanilla scent open on it for much of the year. The plant serves little purpose beyond tinder. It fed sacred blazes and the fires called need-fires, likely because it grew in plenty. Folk belief said that a glamour leads people to take furze's gold for true metal. They fill their pockets, then find a litter of petals at home.

okr.objective: furze is the symbolic bog plant of Ireland.
key_results: Furze is one of the common bog plants of Ireland.
It carries yellow blossoms for much of the year.
The plant fed need-fires and other sacred blazes.
Under a glamour, people mistake furze gold for metal.
